questions.question: What are ARIA roles, states, and properties? Give common examples.
questions.title: ARIA Roles, States & Properties — Basics and Common Use
questions.direct_answer:
What are ARIA roles, states, and properties? Give common examples.

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the browser pipeline, framework hooks, and user-visible outcomes), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Role (e.g., button, dialog, tablist), states (aria-expanded, aria-checked), properties (aria-label, aria-describedby); roles override native semantics.

**Classic weak answer:** Adding role="button" to a div instead of using a <button> — requires keyboard handling, focus, and disabled state manually.

**Senior finish:** Quote the first rule of ARIA (don't use if a native element works), show role="dialog" + aria-modal example, and mention ARIA Live Regions.

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **ARIA Roles, States & Properties — Basics and Common Use** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** What are ARIA roles, states, and properties? Give common examples.

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **Role (e.g., button, dialog, tablist), states (aria-expanded, aria-checked), properties (aria-label, aria-describedby); roles override native semantics**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Adding role="button" to a div instead of using a <button> — requires keyboard handling, focus, and disabled state manually**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Quote the first rule of ARIA (don't use if a native element works), show role="dialog" + aria-modal example, and mention ARIA Live Regions**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** Role (e.g., button, dialog, tablist), states (aria-expanded, aria-checked), properties (aria-label, aria-describedby); roles override native semantics
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

sections.title: Trade-offs & senior signal
sections.content:
### Trade-offs interviewers expect you to name

- **Speed vs safety** (types, runtime checks, validation).
- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.
- **Strong answer:** names **adding role="button" to a div instead of using a <button> — requires keyboard handling, focus, and disabled state manually** and what you do instead.

sections.content:
**Open (15–20 seconds):** Restate the question and give the one-sentence definition.

**Body (45–60 seconds):** Walk through **Role (e.g., button, dialog, tablist), states (aria-expanded, aria-checked), properties (aria-label, aria-describedby); roles override native semantics** as a story: what runs, what breaks, what you log/measure.

**Pitfall (15 seconds):** Call out **Adding role="button" to a div instead of using a <button> — requires keyboard handling, focus, and disabled state manually** — interviewers reward honesty about real bugs.

**Finish (15–20 seconds):** Add **Quote the first rule of ARIA (don't use if a native element works), show role="dialog" + aria-modal example, and mention ARIA Live Regions**, then offer a trade-off question back (“do you optimize for TTFB or TTI here?”).

questions.question: When should you use ARIA attributes and when should you avoid them?
questions.title: When to Use ARIA (and When NOT To) — Practical Guidance
questions.direct_answer:
When should you use ARIA attributes and when should you avoid them?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the browser pipeline, framework hooks, and user-visible outcomes), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Prefer native semantics; use ARIA for custom widgets and dynamic states; never redundantly (role="button" on a <button>).

**Classic weak answer:** Sprinkling ARIA on native elements thinking it improves accessibility — often degrades it (double announcements, conflicting roles).

**Senior finish:** Explain 'No ARIA is better than bad ARIA' and quote WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices patterns as the safe source.

interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Explain 'No ARIA is better than bad ARIA' and quote WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices patterns as the safe source
